scope: select the highest-information new data class + market arena for the next prospective program; no data download, no V4 candidates, no backtest, no old 2018+ holdout access

strong_conclusions: price-only public FX M1 is exhausted for the tested intraday classes
several gross-positive families are economically destroyed by execution cost
true microstructure hypotheses remain UNTESTED (old data lacks the info)

old_holdout_firewall.note: the sealed legacy 2018+ FX holdout is NOT used to compare markets; a new program gets its own prospective dev/val/holdout chronology

A_cme_fx_futures.examples: CME major FX futures (6E/6B/6J/6A) + micro FX (M6E/M6B/M6J)
A_cme_fx_futures.data_class: tick-by-tick trades + top-of-book (NBBO); NO full L2/MBP
A_cme_fx_futures.market: centralized CME FX futures (same FX market as V1-V3)

B_cme_equity_futures.data_class: tick-by-tick trades + top-of-book (NBBO); NO full L2/MBP
B_cme_equity_futures.market: centralized CME equity-index futures (DIFFERENT market, not FX)

C_spot_fx_tick.examples: OTC spot FX (EURUSD, GBPUSD, USDJPY, ...) true tick
C_spot_fx_tick.data_class: timestamped bid/ask quote updates (broker feed); NO central order book; trades rarely genuinely available
C_spot_fx_tick.market: fragmented OTC spot FX (same FX market, but no central venue)
C_spot_fx_tick.providers: Dukascopy (M1, not true tick), broker feeds (variable)

D_crypto_l2.examples: BTC/ETH spot + perps on Binance, Coinbase, Kraken, Bybit, BitMEX, Deribit, OKX
D_crypto_l2.data_class: FULL L2 order-book events (add/cancel/modify/execute) + trades (with aggressor side) + top-of-book + funding/OI + options + liquidations
D_crypto_l2.market: centralized crypto exchanges (fragmented ACROSS exchanges; DIFFERENT market, not FX)
D_crypto_l2.fees: explicit per exchange (taker/maker), funding on perps
D_crypto_l2.providers: Tardis.dev (L2/L3, CSV+API), Kaiko (institutional, SOC-2), native exchange APIs (free/cheap)

score_rationale.scientific_value: A=5 (directly answers the V3 question: does FX microstructure add info M1 missed; stays in FX lineage); D=4 (richest microstructure but different market, V3 FX evidence does not transfer); B=3 (different market); C=2 (FX lineage but low quality, can't fully test)
score_rationale.info_content: D=5 (full L2 book events + signed trades + top-of-book); A/B=3 (trades + top-of-book, no full L2); C=2 (fragmented)
score_rationale.tie_break: A and D tie on weighted score; A is primary because it follows from the V1/V2/V3 FX evidence (same market, new data class) and is a lower-friction centralized venue; D is the fallback (highest raw information but a different market)

capability_honesty.A_cme_fx_futures: supports TRADE_FLOW + TOP_OF_BOOK + derived (microprice, OFI from trades+quotes); does NOT support DEPTH or BOOK_EVENTS (no full L2)
capability_honesty.B_cme_equity_futures: same as A (trades + top-of-book, no full L2)
capability_honesty.C_spot_fx_tick: supports TOP_OF_BOOK (broker) + partial TRADE_FLOW; does NOT support DEPTH/BOOK_EVENTS (no central book)
capability_honesty.D_crypto_l2: supports ALL classes (full L2 book events + signed trades + top-of-book + depth)

pilot_questions.P1_FLOW_INFORMATION: Does signed trade/quote/depth flow predict subsequent short-horizon price movement beyond price history alone?
pilot_questions.P2_COST_AWARE_CONDITIONAL_EDGE: Does microstructure state identify periods where expected move >> executable spread + fee?
pilot_questions.P3_EVENT_TIME_VS_CLOCK_TIME: Is predictive information clearer in event-time than fixed M1 sampling?
pilot_questions.P4_LIQUIDITY_STATE: Does liquidity depletion/replenishment contain information not captured by M1 range/return/spread?
pilot_questions.P5_ARENA_EFFECT: Do families analogous to the V3 gross-positive/cost-dominated classes become economically plausible in a centralized lower-friction arena?
pilot_questions.note: questions, not strategies; no candidate grids

banned_classes: fake tick features reconstructed from candles
high-turnover mean-reversion without explicit executable-cost conditioning
model_capacity_note: do NOT choose deep learning as the objective; first prove the new information class adds incremental predictive information over a price-history baseline. Later models may include: linear/logistic baselines, state-space/latent-factor, Hawkes/event-process, change-point, sequence, self-supervised event representations, optimal stopping/execution timing. Representation learning is secondary.

minimal_falsification_pilot.instruments: 2-3 liquid FX futures (e.g. M6E EUR/USD, M6J JPY, M6B GBP/USD)
minimal_falsification_pilot.period: bounded, e.g. 12-24 months of tick data
minimal_falsification_pilot.split: frozen chronological dev/val BEFORE outcomes; separately sealed holdout (new program's own chronology, NOT the old 2018+ FX holdout)
minimal_falsification_pilot.comparison: price-only M1 baseline vs new-information model (trades + top-of-book flow features)
minimal_falsification_pilot.execution: executable bid/ask + explicit CME fees + tick size; event-time where appropriate
minimal_falsification_pilot.measure: incremental predictive information (e.g. log-loss / rank-IC beyond baseline) AND economic value (net of executable cost)
minimal_falsification_pilot.answers: DOES THE NEW DATA CLASS ADD INFORMATION? (not: can we find a profitable strategy by searching enough parameters?)
minimal_falsification_pilot.fail_fast: if the new-information model adds no incremental predictive information over the price-only baseline on dev+val, STOP - the data class is not worth a full program

data_split_policy.old_2018_fx_holdout: NOT part of the new program; remains sealed
data_split_policy.no_backward_validation: never discover on later data and validate backwards on the old 2018 holdout
data_split_policy.roles_fixed_before: every role fixed before downloading/inspecting outcomes where operationally feasible
data_split_policy.pre_existing_exposure: none assumed; document any unavoidable exposure at the capability-contract gate

resource_plan.pilot_footprint: 2-3 instruments x 12-24 months ~ 5-50 GB (fits on disk, streamed, never full-history in RAM)
resource_plan.ram_requirement: 16 GB Mac M5 sufficient for streaming/predicate-pushed Parquet; no full-history RAM load
resource_plan.disk_requirement: ~100 GB for the pilot; ~1-2 TB for a full multi-year multi-instrument program
resource_plan.cpu_requirement: CPU-only is sufficient for the pilot (no A100 needed); A100 optional later for sequence/embedding models
resource_plan.a100_useful: unnecessary for the pilot; useful only if later sequence/embedding models are justified
resource_plan.storage_format: partitioned Parquet (by instrument/date) with streaming, predicate pushdown, bounded caches; event-native schema (ts_us, price, size, side, bid/ask, bid/ask size)

decision.why_primary_dominates: A is the only arena that (1) stays in the FX market so the V1/V2/V3 evidence directly transfers, (2) provides true microstructure (trades + top-of-book) to test the untested microstructure hypotheses, and (3) is a centralized lower-friction venue that directly addresses the V3 cost-dominated lesson. D has richer raw information (full L2) but is a different market, so the V3 FX evidence does not transfer; it is the fallback if CME FX futures data is unavailable/too costly.

not_selected.B_cme_equity_futures: same data class as A but a different market (equity indices); the V3 FX evidence does not transfer
not_selected.C_spot_fx_tick: fragmented OTC, no central order book, variable quality, hard to model execution; cannot fully test microstructure

next_gate_scope: define and freeze data semantics / acquisition for the selected arena (contract specs, provider, schema, coverage, cost, the new dev/val/holdout chronology). DO NOT download the full dataset, materialize V4 candidates, or run a backtest in this session.
